Messages.Author: Jim Vamp
Messages.Body:
Question: When do the costs of cards actually get paid? For example, you
don't lose the cost of equipment if the action is blocked. What about
modifiers? If the bleed is blocked, do you still pay the conditioning
cost. During combat do you pay the strike cost before you lose your
blood (i.e. my vamp has 1 blood and I want to play aggr. hand damage that
costs 1 blood, do I get the card and then go to torpor, or lose the blood
then not be able to play the card).

Messages.Author: Shane Travis
Messages.Body:
Jim "Vamp (jim....@paonline.com) wrote:

: Question: When do the costs of cards actually get paid? For example, you

: don't lose the cost of equipment if the action is blocked.

Correct.

: What about modifiers?

All modifiers and reaction cards are paid for when they are played.
The cost for action cards is only payd if the action is successful.

: If the bleed is blocked, do you still pay the conditioning cost.

If one had played the Conditioning before the 'declare blockers' phase,
then yes; you still pay for it.

(If he had declined to block and then you conditioned the bleed, he does
not get another chance to block.)

: During combat do you pay the strike cost before you lose your

: blood (i.e. my vamp has 1 blood and I want to play aggr. hand damage that
: costs 1 blood, do I get the card and then go to torpor, or lose the blood
: then not be able to play the card).

The cost for strikes is paid when the card is used. In the above example,
that means you would pay one blood to use the card (reducing the vampire
to 0 blood) and then take a point during strike resolution, sending the
vampire to torpor.

Messages.Author: Lion RAR
Messages.Body:
When using conditioning, you needn't play it until your pray has declined
to block. Although, after you play it, your pray still has the option to
misdirect or deflect your bleed if possible.

In combat, you pay the blood for a strike, when you strike, even if it is
not successful.
For Wolf Claws and Claws of the Dead, you pay after strikes but before
damage resolution. (When it's too late to dodge but not too late to
prevent.)

Just MHO

Rich

Messages.Author: Richard Mines
Messages.Body:
In article <4c7h9t$n...@news.paonline.com>, jim....@paonline.com says...

>
>
>Question: When do the costs of cards actually get paid? For example, you

>don't lose the cost of equipment if the action is blocked. What about
>modifiers? If the bleed is blocked, do you still pay the conditioning
>cost. During combat do you pay the strike cost before you lose your

>blood (i.e. my vamp has 1 blood and I want to play aggr. hand damage that
>costs 1 blood, do I get the card and then go to torpor, or lose the blood
>then not be able to play the card).

You always get the blood back for action / equipment etc if the action is
blocked. Although this is also true for modifiers it shouldn't happen - you
only slap on the Conditioning after they've accepted the bleed so if it's
blocked, you don't play it. In combat damage resolution obviously comes after
strike declaration. Hence, if you've got a vamp on 1 point who wants to use
Wolf Claws you'll have to play the Wolf Claws at or before strike declaration.
This takes the vamp down to 0 blood and hence it'll torpor from any damage
from the other guy. If you waited until damage resolution to play the Wolf
Claws, you'd already be on 0 blood and hence couldn't pay the 1. Thus
youwouldn't torpor but neither would the other vamp. Hope this makes sense.

Richard

My understanding is that the order for declaring responses to actions (or
master cards or whatever) is prey, predator, and then any other Meth
clockwise from the acting Meth. So a Meth you is the grandprey of the
acting Meth would be able to act after the Prey and Pred of the acting
Meth failed to block (either by declaring no block or not completing due
to stealth), and before any other Meth could choose to act.

: Then my second question is can the minions of the target of say
a directed
: action use eagle sight to block a action the Meth has already declined
to block?

Eagles sight at the superior allows an attempt to block any action, so
yes, it would allow another Meth to block a directed action not directed
at them. Some examples: you could use Eagles sight to block a vote if you
are not the pred or prey of the vote caller, to block a bleed against
another Meth, to stop a Grave robbing etc.

I hope this helps

>blocked, you don't play it. In combat damage resolution obviously comes after
>strike declaration. Hence, if you've got a vamp on 1 point who wants to use
>Wolf Claws you'll have to play the Wolf Claws at or before strike declaration.

^^^^^^^^^^^
Between Choose Strike and Resolve Strike, actually.

>This takes the vamp down to 0 blood and hence it'll torpor from any damage
>from the other guy. If you waited until damage resolution to play the Wolf
>Claws, you'd already be on 0 blood and hence couldn't pay the 1. Thus
>youwouldn't torpor but neither would the other vamp. Hope this makes sense.

The actual order is:

Acting Minion chooses strike (pays cost)
Blocking Minion chooses strike (pays cost)
Either or both minions play Claws (and pay costs)
Any S:CE resolves, terminating the sequence.
Any Strike: Dodge resolves, cancelling the opposing strike.
All non-First Strike strikes are resolved.
Damage (if any) is healed/prevented.
All other strikes are resolved.
Damage (if any) is healed/prevented.

Messages.Author: Shane Travis
Messages.Body:
Steven Bauer (sba...@cso.geg.mot.com) wrote:

: There is no rule that you must wait till your opponent declines to

: block to play action mods. You can use that Conditioning to get you
: opponent to block the minion you want him to block. And as you said if
: blocked no cost is paid.

This is a misprint in the VTES printed rules which has been officially
errata'd on the Net, and (IIRC) will be cleared up in an issue of
Duellist as well.

Action Modifiers and Reactions are paid for when they are used, whether
or not the action/block is successful. Action cards themselves are only
paid for when the action becomes successful.

Example:
A: bleeds B
B: Declines to block
A: slaps down conditioning, pays for conditioning.
B: plays Deflection, sending bleed over to C. B pays for Deflection now.
C: Declares a block.
A: Uses a no-cost, +1 stealth card
C: Uses a Telepathic Misdirection (inferior) for +1 intercept. Pays for
TM now.
A: Uses a (theoretical) 1-blood costing +1 stealth card. Pays for it.
C: Cannot come up with more intercept. Bleed successful.

: This lead me to two questions. When does a blocker using eagle sight

: have to announce his/her intention to block? Does he/she get to violate
: ordinary blocking order and go before the blockers prey? Does he/she get
: to go any time during the action?

Eagle's Sight/Anneke (and all other effects) comes into play as follows:
prey, predator, all other methuselahs clockwise from the Methusalah taking
the action. Thus, one cannot use an Eagle's Sight to 'jump in' and block
something before the prey has a chance, even if you want to. You must
'wait your turn' to have a chance to play it.

: Then my second question is can the minions of the target of say a

: directed action use eagle sight to block a action the Meth has already
: declined to block?

This would be acceptable. If one was the acting Meth's prey, and the
target of a (D) action, one could decline to block, wait to see if the
predator was going to use his Anneke to leap in (for example) and then
use your Eagle's Sight in the 'clockwise from the acting meth' part of
the blocking resolution. It is an acceptable way to cycle cards.

(Remember though, in the above example, that even if you do not use your
Eagle's Sight, the Predator still has one last chance to use Anneke - he
is the last person to declare in the clockwise part. In practice, this
gets too time consuming if everyone must declare for every action, and the
whole clockwise bit is usually skipped unless absolutely necessary.)

Messages.Author: Zacour James
Messages.Body:
Just wondering - can you use eagle's sight or Anneke to block your own
actions - the cards do say that you can block any action by any Methuselah.

This may sound useless, but it seems to be one of the few ways to get rid
of Charnas.

-James

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
3j...@qlink.queensu.ca (Zacour James) writes:

>Just wondering - can you use eagle's sight or Anneke to block your own
>actions - the cards do say that you can block any action by any
>Methuselah.

No, for the technical reason that you can't play reaction cards on your
turn.

I would think that under the current official rules, you could Eagle's
Sight yourself if you are acting with the Malkavian Madness Network.
